title: Compact telemetry: route-level budget snapshots + deferred trace tiles (MVP slice)
creator: Priya Patel
description: PRD summary: We need a trimmed, production-safe telemetry surface for the Redwood Console that gives product and infra teams quick visibility into route-level spend and health without the cost and engineering lift of full trace indexing and heavy aggregation. The original scope included an exploratory multi-card cost explorer, full trace drilldowns, anomaly detection, and live per-token tracing. This ticket defines an MVP cut that ships a compact "route budget snapshot" microcard for each top route and a deferred-trace tile that shows a sampled summary with a link to the full trace UI (hosted outside MVP scope). Goals: 1) provide per-route 7-day spend delta, 24h latency P95, and error-rate delta in a compact card; 2) allow on-demand sampling of traces for routes above configured thresholds; 3) keep token and query cost within quotas for customers and reduce backend indexing requirements for the first release.
requirements_clarifications: Microcard fields: route name, top cost contributor (model+variant), 7d spend, 24h P95 latency, 24h error rate, delta indicator vs. baseline
Default sample policy: only capture traces if error rate > 0.5% or P95 increased by >30% for a route in last 24h
Deferred-trace tile: store a single representative span summary and link to full-trace viewer for expanded analysis (full indexing and deep search out of MVP scope)
No real-time stream of per-token data in MVP; logs are batched hourly and retained for 7 days for the MVP slice
Cost attribution: attribute to model variant where available; if variant unavailable, attribute to model family
UI interactions: microcards are clickable and open a lightweight overlay with top-3 traces sampled and simple timeline; deep dive redirects to dedicated trace console (separate ticket)
Access controls: inherit route visibility from existing Console RBAC; no new roles in MVP
scope_changes_and_mvp_cuts: Cut: anomaly detection and ML-based baselining (defer to post-MVP)
Cut: full-text indexed trace search and tag-based filtering (defer to dedicated tracing project)
Cut: per-token cost heatmaps and token-level attribution (defer to Optimize integration later)
Cut: continuous real-time trace ingestion; replace with threshold-triggered sampling to control storage and compute cost
Added: a compact card UI pattern and a simple sampling policy editor (toggle + threshold numbers) to give customers minimal control
acceptance_criteria: Each route microcard renders in under 300ms for customers with <=100 routes in their account
Microcard metrics match backend aggregated values within 2% for spend and within 5% for latency percentiles in our test datasets
Deferred-trace tile returns representative sampled trace summary within 2s of click for sampled routes
Sampling policy respects thresholds and never records traces for routes below thresholds in production traffic tests
Feature flag gate exists to toggle compact telemetry per-organization; default ON for internal dogfood orgs and OFF for GA until rollout
E2E test coverage includes a smoke test asserting microcard load and a load test that demonstrates backend cost per 1000 routes stays under target budget
Product docs and quickstart (Confluence) written and linked from the console card; acceptance requires doc link present
tradeoffs: Using threshold-triggered sampling reduces storage and compute costs but will miss subtle regressions that only appear in low-volume routes
Providing only a compact snapshot reduces time-to-ship and frontend complexity at the cost of fewer exploratory options in the initial release
Deferring deep trace indexing avoids large infra work but requires customers to use external trace viewer for advanced queries
decisions: Decision: ship microcards + deferred-trace tile as the minimal usable telemetry surface for Q1 MVP
Decision: sampling thresholds are user-editable but default conservative values are provided to protect cost; policy lives in console settings
Decision: attribute cost to model variant first, falling back to model family to avoid introducing taxonomy mapping work in MVP
rollout_plan: Gate behind feature flag and enable for internal teams (dogfood) for 2 weeks
Enable for 10 pilot customers via invites and monitor cost delta and error rates for 30 days
If pilot metrics are within targets, expand to 25% of customers, then 100% over two weeks
If backend cost exceeds target or sampling misses critical regressions, rollback flag and re-evaluate with telemetry team
